result.summary: Sets explicit permissions: contents: read on the GitHub Actions CI workflow. This restricts the default GITHUB_TOKEN to read-only access for workflow jobs.
result.problem: CI workflow permissions currently rely on Bitcoin Core's repository-level default setting of read-only. In contributor forks where repository defaults may grant broader write permissions, CI runs execute with unnecessary token privileges.
evidence: PR description: 'On this repository the token is already read-only, through the repository's default... the setting now lives in the workflow and also holds in forks, where each owner sets the default.'
PR description cites precedent in bitcoin-core/secp256k1#1964.
result.scope_notes: Small 3-line addition to a CI workflow file. Diff was not provided in the prompt metadata.
result.card: Sets explicit contents: read permissions on the GitHub Actions CI workflow. This enforces least privilege directly in the workflow definition rather than relying on repository-level default permissions, ensuring contributor forks do not run CI jobs with unneeded write access. It improves CI security posture and does not touch any node software code.

risk.why: A mistake could break CI workflow execution if a job legitimately requires write token access.
